lines.text: You Didn't Know People Used to Cut Coins Into Pieces.
What if I told you that people once cut their money into pieces… and those pieces were still worth something?
But hundreds of years ago, that was actually a way to make change.
One of the most famous coins in the world was the Spanish silver dollar.
People called it the "Piece of Eight."
Because it was worth eight smaller units of currency.
And when smaller coins were hard to find, people sometimes cut silver coins into pieces.
Imagine having a pizza divided into eight slices.
Each slice represents part of the original value.
Have you ever heard someone say "two bits"?
That old expression for 25 cents comes from the Spanish dollar's eight-part value.
Two out of eight parts equals one quarter!
So before credit cards, ATMs, and digital payments… people sometimes made change by literally cutting silver.
Imagine trying that with your debit card today.
You didn't know that about money.
